column1: Tab 6 — Demand Type -> NUCRIPCE Driver Mapping

When the user states a demand/activity (Screen S12), the backend should classify it against these demand-type characteristics, then tag the matching NUCRIPCE driver(s). A single demand can carry more than one driver tag (e.g. a presentation is both Urgency and Collaboration).

column2: User indicates 'first time', 'never done this before', or activity type not in their history
column4: Using a new software tool for the first time

column2: Timeline (Tab 4) = T0/T1/T2 AND user indicates a consequence for delay
column4: Presentation due in 5 hours; assignment due tomorrow

column2: Demand description implies multiple stages, analysis, or problem-solving
column4: Designing a solution, writing an essay, debugging code

column2: User indicates 'I've done this before' or activity matches a recurring pattern in their history
column4: Weekly report, regular chores, known workflow

column2: Cross-reference with user's stored interests/preferences (if provided) or explicit 'I enjoy this'
User indicates personal significance ('this matters to me', 'this is for my future')
column4: Personal project, cause-related volunteering, career-defining task

column2: Demand description includes meeting, presenting to, collaborating with, or responding to others
column4: Team meeting, presentation, group assignment, replying to a colleague

column2: Demand description implies finding out, comparing, or understanding new information
column4: Researching a topic, comparing options, studying for an exam

column2: User lists more than one activity, or says 'everything' / 'I don't know where to start'
column3: Tag each demand separately; only the ONE the user picks proceeds (Tab 7 pattern 22)
column4: Three deadlines this week; dinner, homework and an email at once

column2: Demand set by a manager, tutor or family member rather than chosen
column3: Tags as normal; engine softens language and offers choice of order (reduces demand-avoidance)

column2: Same demand logged 3+ times without starting, or user says 'I've been putting this off'
column3: Routine or Novelty hook + Execute 2-minute start (pattern 17)
column4: Booking a GP appointment put off for weeks

column2: User needs to stop one thing and start another
column4: Moving from coursework to a shift

column2: User needs to stop (hyperfocus exit, sleep, end of day)
column4: 'I need to stop working and sleep'

column1: Asking for help or an adjustment
column2: User needs to request support, an extension or a reasonable adjustment
column4: Asking for extra time; asking to work from home on a flare day

column1: Recurring personal practice (prayer times, daily ritual, meditation habit)
column2: User saves a practice in My Practices with a schedule, or sets Timeline TR with a practice type
column3: Routine (+ Passion if the user marks it as meaningful); Urgency from the next occurrence only
column4: Morning devotion; midday prayer; evening meditation; Sunday reflection

column1: Reflective work required by a course or job (reflective log, placement reflection, supervision or appraisal prep, PDP)
column2: Demand text mentions reflection, reflective log, supervision, appraisal or portfolio
column3: Challenge + Routine (+ Collaboration if for a supervisor or assessor); Urgency from the timeline. Done through Execute and Express; the Reflect pathway can supply the user's saved reflections only if the user chooses.
column4: Nursing placement reflective log; supervision notes; annual appraisal form

column1: Preparing for a significant event (interview, exam, assessment, medical appointment)
column3: Urgency + Challenge (+ Novelty if first time; + Collaboration if others are involved). Meditate (settle) and Adapt (plan the setting) are the usual supports.
column4: Job interview tomorrow; first day on placement; hospital appointment this afternoon

column1: Worked example from the founder's scenario: “Prepare a presentation at a meeting, within 5 hours” → tags: Urgency (T1 timeline, real consequence) + Collaboration (presenting to others) + Challenge (multi-stage: content + structure + delivery). These three tags carry forward into Tab 7's Recommendation Matrix.
